key_insight: LLM agents often over-scope simple tasks, and the paper shows they can save large amounts of work by estimating the minimum needed execution path before acting.
engineering_relevance: For software and workflow automation, task-aware execution can reduce token use, file reads, and runtime cost while preserving task success.
method: Define minimum-sufficient execution and the Agent Cognitive Redundancy Ratio (ACRR).
Propose E3: Estimate the task scope, Execute a minimal path, then Expand only if verification fails.
Validate on a controlled benchmark and a real-model editing harness with pytest-based grading.
evidence_signal: On MSE-Bench with 121 deterministic edits, E3 matched 100% success while reducing cost by 85%, tokens by 91%, and inspected files by 92%; a live gpt-4o harness showed the same leaner behavior at comparable success.
watch_item: The real-model result included a provider rate-limit shortfall, so deployment reliability still depends on API stability and robust fallback handling.
paper_title: Do AI Agents Know When a Task Is Simple? Toward Complexity-Aware Reasoning and Execution
